sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.q: In triangle $ABC$, the angle bisector from $A$ meets side $BC$ at point $D$, dividing it such that $BD=6$ and $DC=9$. If $AB=8$, find $AC$, using the angle bisector theorem ($\frac{BD}{DC}=\frac{AB}{AC}$).
Find the exact area of a regular hexagon with side length 4.
questions.answer: Step 1: A regular hexagon is partitioned into 6 congruent equilateral triangles of side length $s = 4$. Step 2: Area of one equilateral triangle: $A_1 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}s^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(4^2) = 4\sqrt{3}$ Step 3: Total area of hexagon: $A = 6 \times 4\sqrt{3} = \mathbf{24\sqrt{3}} \approx 41.57$
questions.explanation: Step 1: A regular hexagon is partitioned into 6 congruent equilateral triangles of side length $s = 4$. Step 2: Area of one equilateral triangle: $A_1 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}s^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(4^2) = 4\sqrt{3}$ Step 3: Total area of hexagon: $A = 6 \times 4\sqrt{3} = \mathbf{24\sqrt{3}} \approx 41.57$

questions.q: A solid consists of a cylinder of radius 3 and height 8, topped with a hemisphere of the same radius. Find the total volume, in terms of $\pi$.
questions.answer: Cylinder volume: $\pi r^2h=\pi(9)(8)=72\pi$. Hemisphere volume: $\frac{2}{3}\pi r^3=\frac{2}{3}\pi(27)=18\pi$. Total volume: $72\pi+18\pi=90\pi$.
questions.explanation: Cylinder volume: $\pi r^2h=\pi(9)(8)=72\pi$. Hemisphere volume: $\frac{2}{3}\pi r^3=\frac{2}{3}\pi(27)=18\pi$. Total volume: $72\pi+18\pi=90\pi$.

This question has two parts. A circle has radius 10. A chord is drawn 6 units from the center. (a) Find the length of the chord, using the relationship between the radius, the distance from center to chord, and half the chord length (a right triangle relationship). (b) Find the area of the minor segment cut off by this chord, to the nearest whole number, given that the central angle subtended by the chord is approximately $106.3^\circ$ and $\sin(106.3^\circ)\approx0.960$.
questions.answer: (a) Half the chord length: $\sqrt{10^2-6^2}=\sqrt{100-36}=\sqrt{64}=8$. Full chord length: $16$. (b) Segment area = sector area − triangle area. Sector area: $\frac{106.3}{360}\times\pi(10)^2\approx0.2953\times314.16\approx92.8$. Triangle area: $\frac{1}{2}(10)(10)\sin(106.3^\circ)\approx50(0.960)=48$. Segment area: $92.8-48\approx45$.
questions.explanation: (a) Half the chord length: $\sqrt{10^2-6^2}=\sqrt{100-36}=\sqrt{64}=8$. Full chord length: $16$. (b) Segment area = sector area − triangle area. Sector area: $\frac{106.3}{360}\times\pi(10)^2\approx0.2953\times314.16\approx92.8$. Triangle area: $\frac{1}{2}(10)(10)\sin(106.3^\circ)\approx50(0.960)=48$. Segment area: $92.8-48\approx45$.

questions.q: An equilateral triangle has side length 10. Find its height and area, using the fact that the height splits it into two 30-60-90 triangles.
questions.target: The 30-60-90 and 45-45-90 triangles in composite figures
questions.answer: The height corresponds to the longer leg of a 30-60-90 triangle with hypotenuse 10 and shorter leg 5: height $=5\sqrt{3}$. Area $=\frac{1}{2}(10)(5\sqrt{3})=25\sqrt{3}$.
questions.explanation: The height corresponds to the longer leg of a 30-60-90 triangle with hypotenuse 10 and shorter leg 5: height $=5\sqrt{3}$. Area $=\frac{1}{2}(10)(5\sqrt{3})=25\sqrt{3}$.

questions.q: A square is inscribed in a circle of radius 5. Find the side length of the square, using the fact that the diagonal of the square equals the diameter of the circle.
questions.answer: Diameter $=2(5)=10$. For a square, diagonal $=s\sqrt{2}$, so $s\sqrt{2}=10$, giving $s=\frac{10}{\sqrt{2}}=5\sqrt{2}$.
questions.explanation: Diameter $=2(5)=10$. For a square, diagonal $=s\sqrt{2}$, so $s\sqrt{2}=10$, giving $s=\frac{10}{\sqrt{2}}=5\sqrt{2}$.

sections.heading: Part III — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Challenging & Cross-Lesson Synthesis (15–20)

questions.q: Find the measure of each interior angle and each exterior angle of a regular octagon.
questions.target: Regular polygon interior and exterior angles
questions.answer: Sum of interior angles of an $n$-gon: $(n-2)180^\circ$. For $n=8$: $(6)(180^\circ)=1080^\circ$. Each interior angle: $\frac{1080^\circ}{8}=135^\circ$. Each exterior angle (supplementary to the interior angle): $180^\circ-135^\circ=45^\circ$.
questions.explanation: Sum of interior angles of an $n$-gon: $(n-2)180^\circ$. For $n=8$: $(6)(180^\circ)=1080^\circ$. Each interior angle: $\frac{1080^\circ}{8}=135^\circ$. Each exterior angle (supplementary to the interior angle): $180^\circ-135^\circ=45^\circ$.

questions.q: This question has three parts. A running track consists of a rectangle with two semicircular ends. The rectangle is 80 meters long and 40 meters wide, and the semicircles are attached to the two 40-meter-wide ends. (a) Find the radius of each semicircle. (b) Find the total perimeter (distance around) the track, in terms of $\pi$. (c) Find the total enclosed area of the track shape, in terms of $\pi$.
questions.target: A multi-part composite figure and circle problem
questions.answer: (a) The semicircles are attached to the 40-meter ends, so the diameter of each semicircle is 40, giving radius $=20$. (b) Perimeter $=2(\mathrm{rectangle\ length})+2(\mathrm{semicircle\ arc\ length})$. The two semicircles together form one full circle's circumference: $2\pi(20)=40\pi$. Total perimeter: $2(80)+40\pi=160+40\pi$ meters. (c) Area $=\mathrm{rectangle\ area}+\mathrm{combined\ semicircle\ area}$. Rectangle area: $80\times40=3200$. The two semicircles together form one full circle: $\pi(20)^2=400\pi$. Total area: $3200+400\pi$ square meters.
questions.explanation: (a) The semicircles are attached to the 40-meter ends, so the diameter of each semicircle is 40, giving radius $=20$. (b) Perimeter $=2(\mathrm{rectangle\ length})+2(\mathrm{semicircle\ arc\ length})$. The two semicircles together form one full circle's circumference: $2\pi(20)=40\pi$. Total perimeter: $2(80)+40\pi=160+40\pi$ meters. (c) Area $=\mathrm{rectangle\ area}+\mathrm{combined\ semicircle\ area}$. Rectangle area: $80\times40=3200$. The two semicircles together form one full circle: $\pi(20)^2=400\pi$. Total area: $3200+400\pi$ square meters.

questions.q: Find the measure of each exterior angle of a regular hexagon.
questions.answer: The sum of all exterior angles of any convex polygon is $360^\circ$. For a regular hexagon with $n = 6$ equal sides: $\mathrm{Exterior\ angle} = \frac{360^\circ}{n} = \frac{360^\circ}{6} = \mathbf{60^\circ}$
questions.explanation: The sum of all exterior angles of any convex polygon is $360^\circ$. For a regular hexagon with $n = 6$ equal sides: $\mathrm{Exterior\ angle} = \frac{360^\circ}{n} = \frac{360^\circ}{6} = \mathbf{60^\circ}$

questions.q: In $\Delta  ABC$, the circumcenter lies on the midpoint of the longest side. What type of triangle is $\Delta  ABC$?
questions.answer: By Thales's theorem, the circumcenter of a triangle lies on a side if and only if the triangle is a right triangle, where the hypotenuse is the diameter of the circumcircle.

In $\Delta  ABC$, medians intersect at the centroid $G$. If median $AM$ has length $18$ cm, what is the length of $AG$?
questions.answer: The centroid divides each median in a $2:1$ ratio from vertex to midpoint: $AG = \frac{2}{3} AM = \frac{2}{3}(18) = 12$ cm.
